text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's main opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) leader Ivan Kostov demanded the resignation of Interior minister Nikolai Dobrev after the Military prosecutor's office said it had found enough evidence to support Kostov's complaint of bugging the phones of opposition leaders at the UDF headquarters. @

-- The Sofia district court ruled a four-month suspended jail sentence for the editor-in-chief of Noshten Trud daily Plamen Kamenov and ruled that its publisher should pay 200,000 levs to the chief prosecutor Ivan Tatarchev as a compensation for moral damages caused by an article in February 1993.
-- Opposition deputy Edvin Sugarev said a criminal investigation should be launched against Prime Minister Zhan Videnov and seven other senior state officials on charges of corruption. @
-- Bulgaria's Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov said an exchange rate of 400 to 500 levs per dollar was assumed in the 1997 budget draft to accomodate the implementation of a currency board system.
-- Bulgaria's deputy prime minister Roumen Gechev said the Belgian chemical company Solvay SA will buy 60 percent of the Bulgarian soda ash producer Sodi-Devnya for $160 million.

-- The International Monetary Fund (IMF) had suggested a shuffle of the Bulgarian National Bank's board ahead of the planned introduction of a currency board system in the country, a Bulgarian member of parliament said, quoting an IMF official.
-- The main opposition Union of Democratic Forces organised a protest rally in Sofia on Thursday to demand the resignation of the Socialist party government.
-- The central bank said it would plead against a ruling by the Sofia City Court against its bid to seek insolvency for Bulgaria's First Private Bank. @
-- The International Atomic Energy Agency will extend some $1.4 billion to fund six projects in the Bulgarian energy sector over the next two years, a senior Bulgarian energy official said.

-- Total production of goods and services in Bulgaria's state and private sectors in November fell a real 10 percent year-on-year, the National Statistics Institute said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
